insider_note: Here S₁₁ is asked for as a length, so the square root IS taken. The power of a point is S₁₁ itself, with no square root, and mixing the two is the usual error.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the tangent length as √S₁₁
steps.margin_note: One mark. A length is asked for, so the square root is part of the answer.
steps.memory_tip: Tangent length = √S₁₁. Power of a point = S₁₁ with no root.
lines: Length of the tangent from (1, 3) to
steps.why: The tangent from an external point, the radius to the point of contact and the line to the centre form a right-angled triangle, and Pythagoras on it gives the tangent length as √S₁₁.
common_mistakes: Using the distance to the centre as the tangent length.

steps.label: Substitute and evaluate
steps.margin_note: Second mark. S₁₁ = 9 is positive, so the point is outside the circle and a real tangent exists.
steps.why: S₁₁ comes out positive, which confirms the point is outside the circle — a negative value would mean there is no real tangent from it.
common_mistakes: Reporting the answer as 9 rather than 3.
